pr_title: eth/filters: return error if toBlock > latest block
pr_body:
Return an error if the requested block range is not available instead of just ignoring an tracing to latest

closes: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/26101

issue_context.title: FR: Return error if logs toBlock is in the future
issue_context.body:
# Rationale

When requesting logs via `eth_getLogs` if the `toBlock` is set to a block in the future that the node does not have (`toBlock > blockNumber`) then the node should return an error.

Currently, the node would return the logs it has (`fromBlock -> "latest"`), ignoring the fact that `toBlock` is in the future, and there would be no indication to the user that there was a problem or issue with their request.

If you are load balancing requests across nodes for instance, you might ask for logs from a block that one of the nodes doesn't have yet and there's no way to detect there was a problem, there is just a lack of logs for the future blocks, detecting that in code is essentially impossible, especially if there really were no logs for a block.

# Implementation

The Avalanche C chain client has this feature, if you request logs for a block in the future, it will return an error instead of silently continuing and returning invalid results.
